Hi modders! My code is really messy since I had only 4 days to make this initially. Sorry! I'll try my best to guide you through some stuff if you want to make a mod. If you have any questions feel free to ask.


-------------------------
PLAYER MOVEMENT:
-------------------------
- Player movement is all under the "Move (fence?)" custom block in the Player sprite. Keypresses are detected in "when I recieve Tick - Player" using "KEY X" and "KEY Y" variables, and the mobile joystick also uses those variables.
- Default player speed is set in the "speed" variable, under "when I receive reset".


-------------------------
LEVELS AND WAVES:
-------------------------

- The waves in each level are defined by 4 lists: WAVES - TO SPAWN, WAVES - INTRO, WAVES - SPAWN SPEED MODIFIER, and WAVES - TIMER. 

- WAVES - TO SPAWN lists how many of each hazard hazard to spawn. After spawning everything in a random order it will go back and spawn everything again. The format of the list is as follows: for each hazard type, a two-digit number (ex. 01, 02, 11, 67) is written followed by the single-character code for that hazard (m = meteor, k = crack, c = car, z = zombie horde). The item# in the list is simply the level.

For example, if you wanted a level to spawn both cars and meteors, with twice as many cars as meteors, you would do something like "01m02c". This will shuffle one meteor and two cars into a "queue", which will be run through and repeated. Since the ratio of meteors to cars would be 1:2, there would be twice as many cars.

- WAVES - INTRO lists a specific order of hazards to start off certain levels. This is completely optional and is usually used to subtly teach a new mechanic. The format is as follows: each hazard is represented by a single-character code, same as the WAVES - TO SPAWN list. However, rather than using numbers to specify how many of something to spawn, it is just a string of hazards. 

For example, if you wanted to start off a level with two meteors and then a car before kicking off the main level, you would do "mmc".

- WAVES - SPAWN SPEED MODIFIER lists modifiers for how fast hazards should spawn. Experiment with this yourself to see what a good value is.

- WAVES - TIMER lists simply how long the countdown should be for each level.

- The last level that is scrolling is kinda hard to modify... I recommend leaving it as is. If you want a challenge though, feel free to give it a go.



-------------------------
NEW HAZARDS:
-------------------------

- This one's probably the most complicated.

- The first step is to create a costume for the new hazard as well as any animations, particles, and effects

- To implement the spawning of the hazard, put another if else into the "Spawn Hazard" custom block in the hazards sprite. For the if condition, use "selected hazard = (new single-character code)". Inside the if, put a "set type to (costume name of the main costume)" and "create clone of myself". If the hazard has a telegraph that is separate from the hazard itself, make sure to set type to the costume name of the telegraph.

- Also put the positioning of the hazard here, before the clone is created. if it is something that should spawn differently on and off the crosswalk, use the "Pick Random Position on Crosswalk" custom block. This makes the hazard only spawn on the crosswalk. The input is if the hazard should be forced to spawn in front of the player.

- If the hazard should also be able to spawn outside the crosswalk, go to the "Load Hazards" custom block and add "or temp = (single-character code)" to the "if temp = m or temp = k".

- The next step is to actually make the hazard do something. Go to the main action script and add "if type = (previously set type)". Create a new custom block that will contain the thing the hazard will do and put it inside the if. You're now free to code whatever you want the hazard to do, in the new custom block! Just make sure the script either loops infinitely or deletes the clone (if it doesn't, just put an empty forever loop at the end).

- If you want it to spawn something else (like telegraphs spawning the main hazard, particles, effects), just use "set type to (costume name of other thing)" and "create a clone of myself". You can use the "Create Particles" custom block for particles if you like.

- If you want it to do two things simultaneously in different scripts, use the secondary action script (off to the left).

- Finally, for the layering, find "when I receive Order Sprites". If you don't want it to layer by it's y position (things lower on the screen are considered "in front", use another "if type = (type) else" and put the "order sprite by y position" in the else. Then put a different number in the input (higher = layered further back).
